open_questions.question: Which story entries are milestones that are never folded? Proposed: created, completed, approved, sent back, landed or did not land, closed.

problem: Cards and especially the task story (TaskStory.tsx, sentences such as '<agent> is working') carry too much text, so it is hard to understand what is in a task. The operator asked for a redesign based on best UI/UX practice, with animation and finish, in AgentWeave's visual identity (brand/ in the repository is the identity kit).

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-20: mocks are the real components fed fixtures, so applying one is wiring rather than redrawing.
requirements.statement: The redesign is shown first as a mock built from the real board, card, drawer and story components fed fixtures. The mock covers every stage from slice glance and every close from slice loose-tasks. Nothing is wired to live data until the operator approves the mock.

A card shows only: its title; its stage as a glyph and a word; time at stage; the waits-on line when waiting; builder and reviewer; its spec's short tag; a failing-checks marker; and priority only when critical.
Apart from its title, no card shows more than two lines of text at the board's default width.
Description, branch, commits, requirements and acceptance criteria appear in the drawer and never on the card.
A task whose latest checks failed shows, before review, a marker on its card naming how many checks failed. Opening it lists them.

The story view shows a task's history as a timeline of entries, each a glyph, a label of at most six words, the actor and the time. Runs of four or more consecutive routine entries are folded into one that opens. Any entry can be expanded to its full text.
A card changing stage animates the change, finishing within 300 ms. With reduced motion requested by the system, no animation plays and the change still shows.
Colours, type and glyphs come from AgentWeave's identity kit, in both light and dark themes.
No stage or marker is conveyed by colour alone. All card and story text meets WCAG AA contrast in both themes.

in_scope: The task card, the drawer's summary area and the story view
non_goals: What a card's facts are and how they are computed (slices glance, loose-tasks and finding)

summary: Cards and the story view are redesigned around visual state instead of prose, with motion and finish in AgentWeave's visual identity. The design is shown first as a mock built from the real components fed fixtures, and wired to live data once the operator approves it.
